source_text: peccato Adae arbitrium liberum de hominum natura perisse; neminem nisi Dominum Deum nascentium conditorem ... nec a diabolo, sed ab ipso nuptias institutas ... Nec sub nomine gratiae fatum asserimus
pass_a_gloss: that by Adam's sin free decision perished from human nature; that God is not the founder of those being born, or that marriages were instituted by the devil; that under the name of grace they assert fate

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: In introducing his answer to the letter’s brief accusations, Augustine identifies the disputed claims as these: that Adam’s sin destroyed free will in human nature; that God is not the creator of newborn human beings, or that marriage was instituted by the devil rather than by God; and that what his side calls grace is really fate.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
